title: The Price of a Rivalry: Why Big Fixtures Matter Commercially for Delhi Capitals
dek: Big fixtures sell. Delhi Capitals' most frequent opponent is Mumbai Indians; the question is whether those matches deliver more drama than the rest.
excerpt: Delhi Capitals have met Mumbai Indians more than any other side. Those matches have been less close than their other fixtures: the on-field half of a rivalry's commercial value.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Why Rivalries Matter Commercially
body: Rivalry fixtures are the matches that sell out first, draw the biggest audiences and carry the most social conversation. Their commercial value rests on two things: history and drama.
Delhi Capitals' most frequent opponent is {{ev:pr-rival}}, with {{ev:pr-n}} meetings.

sections.heading: Do the Big Fixtures Deliver?
body: {{ev:pr-rc}} of decided matches against MI were close, against {{ev:pr-oc}} of Delhi Capitals' other fixtures. Those matches have produced {{ev:pr-rr}} runs per match, against {{ev:pr-or}} elsewhere.
On this measure, the rivalry fixture has been less tense than the average match; its appeal rests more on history than on finishes.

sections.heading: Most-Played Is Not Always the Fiercest
body: The most frequent opponent is a measurable stand-in for a rivalry, but the rivalry fans feel may be with a different team, shaped by geography, history or a single final.

sections.heading: What the Warehouse Cannot See
body: The CricField warehouse is ball-by-ball cricket data. It contains no ticket demand, audience or social-conversation data, so it cannot measure the commercial side of this question directly.
Pricing a rivalry would need sell-out speed, secondary-market prices and audience figures for each fixture.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: History Plus Drama
body: Delhi Capitals' meetings with MI have a long history; whether they also bring above-average drama is shown in the comparison above.
The commercial premium on the fixture needs demand data to measure.

methodology: CricField measures the cricket a franchise puts on the field; it holds no revenue, attendance, audience, merchandise or social-media data. Commercial ideas in this article are labelled hypotheses with the data needed to test them. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Rivalry = the franchise's most frequent opponent. Close = decided by ten runs or fewer, six balls or fewer to spare, or a super over.
